sources.citation: Suter, Edgar. 2018. Comparative Morphology of the Huon Peninsula Languages (Papua New Guinea). Inaugural-Dissertation, Universität zu Köln. viii+331 pp. (KUPS 9757)
sources.note: Nothing for Momare. Momare data come from Pilhofer 1928 and unpublished Momare texts collected by Steve McEvoy (SIL, Preface p. iii); the comparative phonology is explicitly unwritten. Only reconstructive asides: Huon Tip emphatic pronouns (incl. Momare ja-haʔ 'himself', na-haʔ 'myself') kept *ja 'presumably because the latter bore a heavy stress on the first syllable in discourse' (p. ~107); Kâte-Mape present tense 'presumably had a unitary word accent on the first syllable of the verb root' (p. ~180) -- diachronic conjectures, not a description of Momare stress.

sources.note: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' No Momare OPD, grammar or phonology in the SIL-PNG archive (2013); the 2026 archive search is Cloudflare-blocked from our machine.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1970. Selepet grammar, part I: from root to phrase (with a survey of the Finisterre-Huon languages). PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.note: The stress description (primary stress on the initial syllable of the stress group, secondary stresses on alternate syllables, ch. on phonology/intonation) is for Selepet only. Momare (language 'D') figures only in the Huon Peninsula survey chapter (history: Schmidt's 'Poom' = Momare; lexicostatistics; Eastern Huon Family list).

sources.citation: McEvoy, Steve. 2005. Migabac phonology essentials (in Phonological Descriptions of PNG Languages, SIL-PNG) -- the sister language's description, held in the catalog under miga1241.
sources.note: Describes Migabac stress (sec. 4, primary/secondary levels, alternating pattern); Momare is named only in the Eastern Huon family list (McElhanon 1978); nothing about Momare stress.
